headline: Another strong storm arrives Wednesday night into Thanksgiving with wind advisories from the Strait of Juan de Fuca to Seattle, heavy rain, and widespread coastal flooding at Thursday's high tides, so expect slow holiday travel along I-5.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: Rain keeps moving onshore Tuesday evening and overnight as a weather front pushes inland, with some heavy bands at times. Winds stay gusty this evening, then ease across Puget Sound overnight but remain gusty around the Strait of Juan de Fuca, the San Juans and northern waters, and along the coast, where a Wind Advisory for the north and Grays Harbor coasts and the western and southern Olympic foothills runs until 10 PM. A Winter Weather Advisory covers the Cascades of Whatcom and Skagit counties until 10 PM.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: Winds ease slightly Wednesday and turn more southerly before the next front brings another round of strong south winds late Wednesday night into Thursday. Wind Advisories run 4 PM Wednesday to 11 AM Thursday for the Eastern and Western Strait of Juan de Fuca (Sequim and Port Angeles), Port Townsend, the Lake Crescent/US 101 area, the San Juans, Everett and the North Interior, and the coast, and 8 PM Wednesday to noon Thursday for Seattle, the Eastside, Kitsap, Tacoma, Olympia and the Olympics; gusts of roughly 45–50 mph are expected through Puget Sound (40–45 mph at Sea-Tac) and about 55 mph on the coast, with winds staying up much of Thursday, so allow extra travel time, especially on I-5. The ongoing rain adds another 2–5 inches across the region, most in the Olympics, with a slight chance of thunderstorms Thursday after the front; a Flood Watch runs Wednesday morning through Sunday afternoon for the Olympics and their foothills, Olympia and southern Puget Sound, southern Hood Canal, the Chehalis Valley and the Willapa and Black Hills, where the Skokomish River in Mason County should reach moderate flooding midweek, though no widespread river flooding is expected. In the North Cascades, a Winter Storm Watch late Wednesday night through Thursday afternoon calls for up to 15 inches of snow at Washington Pass and above 5,000 feet.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: Friday brings some easing, and Saturday should be a brief break from rain for most of the area. More storms are forecast from Sunday on as low pressure returns offshore, keeping the weather active into early December.

coast: Very high tides return Thursday just as the next front arrives, bringing widespread coastal flooding to waterfront areas: major flooding is possible at Friday Harbor, Westport and Cherry Point, and moderate flooding at the other tide gauges, including along the Strait of Juan de Fuca. Coastal Flood Watches run late Tuesday night through Wednesday afternoon and again late Wednesday night through Thursday afternoon for the Eastern and Western Strait of Juan de Fuca, Port Townsend, the San Juans, Island County, northern Hood Canal, Kitsap, the Seattle, Everett, Pierce/south King, Skagit/Snohomish and Whatcom shorelines, and the north and Grays Harbor coasts (Tuesday's Coastal Flood Warnings and Advisories end by 3–5 PM). Waves caused significant damage on the Pacific coast Tuesday and can throw large rocks and logs ashore, so stay off jetties and the immediate shoreline; a High Surf Advisory covers the north and Grays Harbor coasts until 4 PM Wednesday. The flood threat eases slightly Friday, but longer-range models hint that weekend low pressure could bring it back. Seas of 15–25 feet ease to 10–15 feet by Thursday afternoon and 6–9 feet Saturday and Sunday, then build above 10 feet Monday. For boaters, a Storm Warning covers the coastal waters until 1 AM Wednesday, then a Gale Warning until 1 PM, then another Storm Warning 1–10 PM Wednesday; Gale Warnings run until 10 PM Wednesday for the east Strait, until 4 PM Tuesday and again 1–10 PM Wednesday for the west Strait (Small Craft Advisory in between), and until 5 AM Wednesday for the northern inland waters and San Juans (then a Small Craft Advisory to 10 PM). Small Craft Advisories also cover the central Strait until 10 PM Tuesday, Puget Sound and Hood Canal until 10 AM Wednesday, and Admiralty Inlet and the Grays Harbor bar until 10 PM Wednesday. Isolated thunderstorms are possible over the coastal waters each afternoon and evening through Thursday, and high pressure should bring a brief break from the wind Friday before winds pick up again next week.
watch_for: Coastal flooding at Thursday's high tides, possibly major at Friday Harbor, Westport and Cherry Point, and moderate along the Strait of Juan de Fuca and Puget Sound.
Strong south winds late Wednesday night into Thursday that could slow Thanksgiving travel along I-5.
Whether weekend low pressure brings coastal flooding back, and the Skokomish River's rise to moderate flood midweek.
confidence: Forecasters are confident in another stormy round Wednesday night into Thursday, with advisories and watches already in place, while the weekend's return of coastal flooding and the timing of next week's storms rest on less certain longer-range model guidance.
